![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14223200/assets/0f178c33254644c5e2e7bf6f3c596df87b1ea2f0b5bfd417c3f279f6c62b1b0d.png)

Consider the circle $S$ and the vector field $F,$ shown above. Let $C$ be any path where $S$ is traversed once in the **clockwise** direction. Which of the following statements are true?

I. ${∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0$

II. ${∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0$

III. ${∮}_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0$
question.worked_solution:
The circulation $Γ$ measures the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along a *closed* curve $C.$
It is given by the formula

$$
Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

We now recall the following:

- If the force works *with* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force helps to push the particle along the path), then ${∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0.$

- If the force works *against* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force impedes the motion of the particle as it moves along the path), then ${∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0.$

With that in mind, let's check each statement.

- Statement I is false, while statement II is true. It's clear from the picture below that $F$ works against the motion of the particle as it moves clockwise along $C.$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14223200/assets/f87d2e735ad58e0b33a813fb91ab202ac0eeaf90575979ea45f954fb7e1d0493.png)

So, $Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0.$

- Statement III is true. It's clear from the picture below that $F$ assists the motion of the particle as it moves counterclockwise along $C.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14223200/assets/102c11f9002e29a3759679c6ff0bd10188908d33eb9cc94a84d900956adc33a5.png)

So, $Γ={∮}_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
